2.doc: MCI Due to Alzheimer’s Disease Infusions
2.title: 🧠 What are AD infusions?
2.content: AD infusions are IV anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies intended to reduce amyloid plaque burden in the brain. They are: . | Used in MCI due to AD | Administered on a regular infusion schedule | Closely monitored due to potential adverse effects | .

4.title: 📋 What to Check Every Visit
4.content: . | MoCa and FAQ completed every 5-6 Months (Please do this!!!) | Current infusion number . | Either the patient will know AND | Please ask staff to contact PA Money on what infusion the patient is currently on | . | Last infusion date | Any missed or delayed doses | Recent MRI results | New neurologic symptoms | Anticoagulant or antiplatelet use | .

5.doc: MCI Due to Alzheimer’s Disease Infusions
5.title: ⚠️ ARIA (Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities)
5.content: ARIA-E (Edema) . | Cerebral edema | May be asymptomatic or symptomatic | . ARIA-H (Hemorrhage) . | Microhemorrhages or superficial siderosis | Increased risk with anticoagulation | . 💗 **Always ask about:** headaches, confusion, dizziness, visual changes, nausea, gait changes, or focal neurologic symptoms.

6.doc: MCI Due to Alzheimer’s Disease Infusions
6.title: 🧠 MRI & Amyloid PET Monitoring
6.content: . | MRIs are performed at scheduled intervals | Imaging determines whether infusions continue, pause, or stop | MRI findings may guide dose or schedule changes | Kisunla Monitoring for ARIA: . | Obtain a recent baseline brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) prior to initiating treatment with KISUNLA. Obtain an MRI prior to the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 7th infusions. If a patient experiences symptoms suggestive of ARIA, clinical evaluation should be performed, including an MRI if indicated. | . | Lequembi Monitoring for ARIA: . | Obtain a recent baseline brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) prior to initiating treatment with LEQEMBI. Obtain an MRI prior to the 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 14th infusions. In general, the MRI should be performed within approximately one week before the scheduled infusion of LEQEMBI and reviewed prior to proceeding with the infusion. If a patient experiences symptoms suggestive of ARIA, clinical evaluation should be performed, including an MRI if indicated. | . | For both amyloid PET scans will be scheduled prior to infusions, 12 months and 18 months to assess pt Centiloid Value before and after to assess efficacy of treatment and whether pt can stop treatment. | .

7.doc: MCI Due to Alzheimer’s Disease Infusions
7.title: 📝 Documentation Tips
7.content: Include: . | Infusion number and tolerance | MRI date and impression | Presence or absence of ARIA symptoms | Any ED visits or hospitalizations | Counseling provided | .

8.doc: MCI Due to Alzheimer’s Disease Infusions
8.title: 👥 Patient & Caregiver Counseling
8.content: Key points: . | Not a cure | Intended to slow disease progression | Safety monitoring is essential | New neurologic symptoms should prompt immediate contact | Don’t forget to do MoCa and FAQ Every 5-6 Months | Pt will Return to clinic every 5 months | .

9.doc: MCI Due to Alzheimer’s Disease Infusions
9.title: 🐰 Key Takeaways
9.content: 💗 Safety and monitoring matter more than speed. | Know the infusion number | Ask ARIA questions every visit | Document MRI status | Involve caregivers | . 🐾 When unsure, escalate questions—infusion safety comes first and please ask staff if confused.

28.title: Established Movement Patient
28.content: Use this checklist for a routine Movement Disorders follow-up visit. Shared Clinic Workflow This guide assumes you are familiar with the general established-patient workflow if your patient has memory concern as well as motor. If you have not already done so, begin with the Memory Disorders – Established Patient Guide if your patient raises concerns for memory. The sections below highlight only the workflow, documentation, and clinical considerations that differ for Movement Disorders patients. Before Dr. Morgan and YOU Enter the Room . | Review the most recent clinic note. | Review the diagnosis and current treatment plan. | Review medication doses and timing. | Review testing completed since the previous visit. | Identify the follow-up concerns from the previous plan. | . During the Patient and Caregiver History Obtain symptom, functional, and safety history . | Ask whether movement symptoms have improved, worsened, or remained stable since the last visit. | Ask about any new or worsening symptoms since the previous visit. | Review current movement disorder medications, including medication timing and adherence. | Ask about medication benefit, wearing off, delayed onset, dose failures, or fluctuating symptoms when applicable. | Ask about dyskinesias, dystonia, or other involuntary movements when applicable. | Ask about medication side effects or concerns. | Ask about falls, balance, gait, freezing, or assistive device use. | Ask about swallowing difficulties, speech changes, sleep, mood, cognition, hallucinations, constipation, urinary symptoms, or autonomic symptoms when relevant. | Ask whether there have been any hospitalizations, emergency department visits, surgeries, or significant medical changes since the last visit. | Review any interval imaging, laboratory studies, or diagnostic testing completed since the previous visit. | Ask about botulinum toxin injections, DBS, focused ultrasound (FUS), or other interval procedures when applicable. | Ask about participation in physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, or regular exercise since the previous visit. | Review any changes in activities of daily living, work status, or quality of life. | Confirm whether the patient is currently driving and ask about any new driving concerns when applicable. | . Presenting the Patient Prepare a concise presentation for Dr. Morgan . | State the patient’s diagnosis and the reason for today’s follow-up visit. | Summarize any significant changes in symptoms since the previous visit. | Review current movement disorder medications, including benefit, wearing off, dyskinesias, side effects, medication timing, and any recent changes. | Report any interval falls, hospitalizations, procedures, or significant medical events. | Summarize any new imaging, laboratory studies, or other diagnostic testing completed since the last visit. | Report the most important neurologic and movement examination findings, emphasizing changes from the previous visit. | Describe any changes in activities of daily living, gait, balance, driving, or quality of life. | Identify the primary clinical question or management issue for today’s visit. | Clarify any uncertain findings or questions with Caty, the fellow, or Dr. Morgan before presenting the patient. | . After the Visit Complete follow-up instructions and documentation . | Confirm Dr. Morgan’s assessment and treatment plan. | Confirm any medication changes, including dosing instructions and titration schedules. | Confirm any referrals, imaging, laboratory studies, procedures, or therapy orders placed during today’s visit. | Confirm when the patient should return to see Dr. Morgan. | Complete the clinic information sheet, including the recommended follow-up timeframe and any testing that should be completed before the next visit. | Return to the patient room, review the treatment and follow-up plan, answer any remaining questions, provide any signed referrals if needed, and direct the patient to the front desk to schedule their next appointment. | . Important Complete all required questionnaires before Dr. Morgan enters the room. Documents to scan should have a patient sticker placed on them (the front). Please place them in the pink folder. Return to Movement Disorders Guides .

30.title: 🧠Established Memory Patient
30.content: Use this checklist for a routine Memory Disorders follow-up visit. Before Dr. Morgan Enters Required intake forms and materials . | Review the most recent clinic note. | Review the diagnosis and current treatment plan. | Review medication changes from the previous visit. | Review testing completed since the previous visit. | Review the most recent MOCA score. Don’t repeat if <=12. Repeat MOCA if done 1 year prior and >12. | Identify the follow-up concerns from the previous plan. | . Patient and Caregiver Update Review the chart and prepare for intake . | Ask whether cognition has improved, worsened, or remained stable. | Ask for specific examples of cognitive changes. | Review basic activities of daily living. | Review instrumental activities of daily living. | Confirm who manages medications and finances. | Confirm whether the patient is driving. | Ask about medication benefit and side effects. | Ask about mood, sleep, hallucinations, behavior, falls, wandering, and safety concerns. | Ask about caregiver concerns and caregiver burden. | Obtain collateral history when available. | Complete the MoCA if requested or due. | Complete the FAQ if requested or due. | Review recent imaging and laboratory results. | Review neuropsychological testing when applicable. | . Presenting the Patient Prepare a concise presentation for Dr. Morgan . | Make sure to have completed the appropriate neurologic examination. | Compare cognition and function with the previous visit. | Prepare a presentation for Dr. Morgan, including medication. | Review last visits plans and what was and was not completed, and the results of the labs/tests if done. | Review last visits MOCA score. | Identify the main treatment or safety concern for today’s visit. | Ask Caty, the fellow, or Dr. Morgan when instructions or findings are unclear. | . After the Visit Complete follow-up instructions and documentation . | Confirm medication changes. | Confirm testing and referrals. | Confirm in how many month or in a year for patient to have a return visit and write it on the clinic informational sheet and give to the patient. | Give the patient any referrals needed with Dr. Morgans signature. If they are digital referrals, they will receive a call to schedule. | . Standard memory follow-up is generally one year with Dr. Morgan or six months in continuity clinic when an earlier visit is needed. If patient MoCa is below 14, ask Dr. Morgan if patient should be released from clinic back to PCP. Follow Dr. Morgan’s specific instructions. Important Complete all required questionnaires before Dr. Morgan enters the room. Documents to scan should have a patient sticker placed on them (the front). Please place them in the pink folder. Return to Memory Disorders Guides .

87.title: New Movement Patient
87.content: Use this checklist for a patient being evaluated in the Movement Disorders Clinic for the first time. Initial visit Movement clinic Checklist General Clinic Workflow The majority of the new patient workflow is shared between the Memory and Movement Disorders clinics. Please review the **Memory Disorders – New Patient Guide** before using this page. The sections below describe only workflow and documentation that differ for Movement Disorders patients. Before Dr. Morgan and YOU Enter the Room Required intake forms and materials . | Review the referral reason. | Review available neurology notes. | Review relevant imaging and testing. | Review the medication list. | Identify the patient’s primary concern. | . During the Patient and Caregiver History Obtain symptom, functional, and safety history . | Review the medication list with patient, relevant to memory, movement, and mood. Disregard all other medications. | Write with a header and bullet list below. One header should be: Current Medications, Trialed Medications. Please the medications where needed, and include dosages, time taken, or reason for stopping medication. | Determine when the symptoms began. | Ask how the symptoms have progressed. | Ask which body area was affected first. | Ask about tremor, stiffness, slowness, abnormal movements, or balance problems. | Ask about falls and use of assistive devices. | Ask about changes in walking. | Ask about swallowing or speech changes. | Ask about sleep symptoms. | Ask about hallucinations or behavioral changes when relevant. | Ask about current and previous treatments. | Ask whether medications improve the symptoms. | Review basic and instrumental activities of daily living. | Confirm whether the patient is driving. | . Presenting the Patient Prepare a concise presentation for Dr. Morgan . | State the patient’s age, handedness (if relevant), and reason for referral. | Summarize the chief complaint and timeline of symptom onset and progression. | Describe the primary movement disorder (e.g., tremor, parkinsonism, dystonia, ataxia, chorea, myoclonus, tics). | Describe how the symptoms affect activities of daily living, work, gait, balance, or quality of life. | Report associated neurologic symptoms (e.g., falls, freezing, dysphagia, hypophonia, autonomic symptoms, cognitive changes, REM sleep behavior disorder) when applicable. | Review current and previous movement disorder medications, including benefit, side effects, wearing off, dyskinesias, and medication timing when applicable. | Summarize relevant imaging or diagnostic studies, including DaTscan, MRI brain, EMG/NCS, genetic testing, or other pertinent testing when available. | Report the most important examination findings. | State your leading differential diagnosis or primary clinical concern, if appropriate. | Identify the primary clinical question or reason for today’s visit. | Clarify any uncertain findings or questions with Caty, the fellow, or Dr. Morgan before presenting the patient. | . After the Visit Complete follow-up instructions and documentation . | Confirm the treatment plan. | Confirm medication changes. | Confirm referrals or testing orders. | Confirm when the patient should return with Dr. Morgan. | Write on clinic information sheet when to follow-up on the visit sheet. Also include any tests needed to be completed before next visit. | Give the patient any referrals needed with Dr. Morgans signature. If they are digital referrals, they will receive a call to schedule. | Return to patient room and give the patient the clinic information sheet, tell them when to return, and to head to the front desk to schedule their next visit. | . Important Complete all required questionnaires before Dr. Morgan enters the room. Documents to scan should have a patient sticker placed on them (the front). Please place them in the pink folder. 89.title: 🧠 New Memory Patient
89.content: Use this guide for a patient’s initial evaluation in the Memory Disorders Clinic. Initial visit Memory clinic Checklist Before Dr. Morgan Enters Required intake forms and materials . | Complete the MoCA using the materials in the purple folder. | Complete the FAQ using the materials in the purple folder. | Complete the PHQ-9 using the materials in the purple folder. | Complete the GAD-7 using the materials in the purple folder. | Bring a pen and clipboard into the room. | For memory patients located in Georgia, obtain the GMN consent form by asking Caty or the social worker. | . Before Entering the Room Review the chart and prepare for intake . | Review the reason for referral. | Review previous neurology, memory clinic, or primary care notes. | Find the most recent brain MRI or CT. | Review available laboratory results. | Review the current medication list. | Identify the family member or caregiver who can provide collateral history. | Review prior cognitive testing, if available. | Identify any testing or referrals that have already been completed. | . During the Patient and Caregiver History Obtain symptom, functional, and safety history . | Determine when the cognitive symptoms began. | Ask whether the symptoms began gradually or suddenly. | Ask how the symptoms have progressed. | Ask for specific examples of short-term memory difficulty. | Ask about repeated questions or repeated conversations. | Ask about missed appointments or difficulty keeping track of dates. | Ask about misplaced belongings. | Ask about difficulty remembering recent events. | Ask about changes in language or word-finding. | Ask about difficulty recognizing people or objects. | Ask about changes in navigation or getting lost. | Ask about changes in judgment, planning, or problem-solving. | Ask about changes in personality or behavior. | Ask about mood, anxiety, depression, or irritability. | Ask about hallucinations or delusions. | Ask about sleep, including dream enactment or excessive daytime sleepiness. | Ask about tremor, stiffness, slowness, gait changes, or falls. | Ask about urinary or bowel changes when relevant. | Obtain collateral history from a family member or caregiver whenever available. | . Function and Safety Review ADLs, IADLs, driving, and supervision . | Review basic activities of daily living. | Review instrumental activities of daily living. | Ask who manages medications. | Ask who manages finances. | Ask whether the patient cooks independently. | Ask whether the patient shops independently. | Ask whether the patient uses a calendar or reminders. | Confirm whether the patient is currently driving. | Ask about recent accidents, tickets, getting lost, or family concerns about driving. | Ask whether the patient lives alone. | Ask whether the patient requires supervision. | Ask about falls, wandering, firearm access, or other safety concerns when relevant. | Ask about caregiver concerns and caregiver burden. | . Examination and Cognitive Testing Complete and review the requested assessment . | Review the MoCA score and areas of difficulty. | Review the FAQ score and reported functional changes. | Review the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 results. | Complete the appropriate neurologic examination. | Assess gait when appropriate. | Identify the most important positive examination findings. | Compare the patient’s reported symptoms with the caregiver’s collateral history. | Identify whether the presentation appears primarily cognitive, psychiatric, functional, neurologic, or mixed. | . Presenting the Patient Prepare a concise presentation for Dr. Morgan . | State the patient’s age and reason for referral. | Summarize the onset and progression of cognitive symptoms. | Provide two or three specific examples of the patient’s cognitive difficulty. | Summarize the caregiver’s collateral history. | Describe changes in ADLs and IADLs. | State who manages medications and finances. | State whether the patient is driving. | Summarize relevant mood, sleep, behavioral, hallucination, gait, or movement symptoms. | Report the MoCA, FAQ, PHQ-9, and GAD-7 scores. | Summarize relevant imaging, laboratory testing, and prior neuropsychological testing. | Report the most important examination findings. | Identify the primary clinical question for the visit. | Ask Caty, the fellow, or Dr. Morgan when instructions or findings are unclear. | . After the Visit Complete follow-up instructions and documentation . | Confirm ordered laboratory testing. | Confirm ordered brain imaging. | Confirm whether neuropsychological testing was ordered. | Confirm any referrals placed during the visit. | Confirm medication recommendations or medication changes. | Confirm when the patient should return to clinic via Dr. Morgan. | Complete the first-patient visit sheet with month (ex: 4 months) and cross out/write down what needs to be done based on plan before the next visit. | Inform the patient that testing should be completed before the follow-up appointment. | Record where the patient should return if the follow-up visit is not with Dr. Morgan. | Return to patient room and give the patient the clinic information sheet, first visit sheet, tell them when to return, and to head to the front desk to schedule their next visit. | . Important Complete all required questionnaires before Dr. Morgan enters the room. Place a patient sticker on the front of all documents that need to be scanned, then place them in the pink folder. Return to Memory Disorders Guides .

91.title: 🧠Second Memory Visit
91.content: Use this checklist for a patient's second Memory Disorders Clinic visit. Initial visit Memory clinic Checklist Before Dr. Morgan Enters Required intake forms and materials . | Review the first clinic note. | Review the prior cognitive testing results. | Review completed laboratory testing. | Review the most recent brain MRI or CT. | Review the most recent MOCA score. Don’t repeat if <=12. Repeat MOCA if done 1 year prior and >12. | Review neuropsychological testing, if completed. | Review the amyloid PET scan, if completed. | Determine whether all requested testing was completed. | . Patient and Caregiver Update Review the chart and prepare for intake . | Ask whether memory symptoms have changed. | Ask about new functional changes. | Review basic and instrumental activities of daily living. | Confirm who manages medications and finances. | Confirm whether the patient is driving. | Ask about mood, sleep, behavior, hallucinations, falls, and safety concerns. | Obtain collateral history from the caregiver when available. | . Presenting the Patient Prepare a concise presentation for Dr. Morgan . | Complete updated cognitive testing when requested. | Prepare a presentation for Dr. Morgan, including medication. | Summarize the onset and progression of cognitive symptoms. | Provide two or three specific examples of the patient’s cognitive difficulty. | Summarize the caregiver’s collateral history. | Describe changes in ADLs and IADLs. | Review last visits MOCA score. | Review last visits plans and what was and was not completed, and the results of the labs/tests if done. | Report the most important examination findings. | Be prepared to discuss the testing results and likely diagnosis. | Ask Caty, the fellow, or Dr. Morgan when instructions or findings are unclear. | . After the Visit Complete follow-up instructions and documentation . | Confirm the diagnosis discussed with the patient and caregiver. | Confirm medication recommendations. | Confirm additional testing or referrals. | Confirm in how many month or in a year for patient to have a return visit and write it on the clinic information sheet and give to the patient. | Give the patient any referrals needed with Dr. Morgans signature. If they are digital referrals, they will receive a call to schedule. | Return to patient room and give the patient the clinic information sheet, tell them when to return, and to head to the front desk to schedule their next visit. | . Confirm whether the patient diagnosis and whether patient should return in six months, one year, or released from clinic based on Dr. Morgan’s instructions. Important Complete all required questionnaires before Dr. Morgan enters the room. Documents to scan should have a patient sticker placed on them (the front). Please place them in the pink folder. Return to Memory Disorders Guides .

93.title: Second Movement Visit
93.content: Use this checklist for a patient's second Movement Disorders Clinic visit. Initial visit Memory clinic Checklist Shared Clinic Workflow This guide assumes you are familiar with the general second-visit workflow. If you have not already done so, begin with the Memory Disorders – Second Visit Guide. The sections below highlight only the workflow, documentation, and clinical considerations that differ for Movement Disorders patients. Before Dr. Morgan and YOU Enter the Room Required intake forms and materials . | Review the previous clinic note. | Review the working diagnosis. | Review tests, imaging, laboratory results, and referrals ordered at the first visit. | Determine whether all requested testing was completed. | Review medication changes made at the first visit. | . During the Patient and Caregiver History Obtain symptom, functional, and safety history . | Ask whether symptoms have improved, worsened, or remained stable. | Ask about new symptoms. | Ask whether the patient started the recommended medications. | Ask whether the medications have helped. | Ask about side effects or wearing off of medication. | Ask about falls, walking, swallowing, speech, and daily functioning. | Confirm whether the patient is driving. | . Presenting the Patient Prepare a concise presentation for Dr. Morgan . | State the patient’s diagnosis and the reason for today’s follow-up visit. | Summarize any significant changes since the last visit, including progression or improvement of symptoms. | Review current movement disorder medications, including medication timing, benefit, wearing off, dyskinesias, adverse effects, and any recent medication changes. | Review any interval events, including falls, freezing, dysphagia, speech changes, hospitalizations, emergency department visits, or new diagnoses. | Report any interval procedures or treatments, including botulinum toxin injections, DBS programming, focused ultrasound (FUS), physical therapy, occupational therapy, or speech therapy, when applicable. | Summarize any new imaging, DaTscan, laboratory results, or diagnostic testing completed since the previous visit. | Report the most important neurologic and movement examination findings, emphasizing changes from the previous visit. | Describe any changes in activities of daily living, mobility, gait, balance, or quality of life. | Identify the primary clinical question or management issue for today’s visit. | Clarify any uncertain findings or questions with Caty, the fellow, or Dr. Morgan before presenting the patient. | . After the Visit Complete follow-up instructions and documentation . | Confirm Dr. Morgan’s assessment and treatment plan. | Confirm any medication changes, including dosing instructions and titration schedules. | Confirm any new referrals, imaging, laboratory tests, or other diagnostic studies ordered today. | Confirm whether additional therapies (e.g., physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, botulinum toxin injections, DBS evaluation, or focused ultrasound evaluation) were recommended, when applicable. | Confirm when the patient should return to see Dr. Morgan. | Complete the clinic information sheet, including the follow-up timeframe and any testing or referrals that should be completed before the next visit. | Provide the patient with any signed paper referrals. Inform the patient that electronic referrals will contact them directly to schedule. | Return to patient room and give the patient the clinic information sheet, tell them when to return (with it writen on the clinic infromation sheet), and to head to the front desk to schedule their next visit. | . Important Complete all required questionnaires before Dr. Morgan enters the room. Documents to scan should have a patient sticker placed on them (the front). Please place them in the pink folder. Return to Movement Disorders Guides .
